newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end up sharply,off peaks.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end up sharply,off peaks.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended a session of active, extremely volatile pit trading sharply higher but off day's price peaks.

Traders said turnover in most pits had slowed by midday as prices carved out and lounged in ranges for the afternoon following a topsy-turvy morning when futures, paced by a startling rally in yen, surged in fits and starts.
"We really got kicked around today," said one exhausted currency futures floor broker after the close.
Trade briefly picked up again in sterling when a fund bid on 1,000 Junes but bought only 600 at the close, brokers said.
Price boards estimated volume at some of the heaviest levels in weeks, with turnover in June yen, marks and Swiss francs shown at roughly 47,000, 46,000 and 31,000 contracts, respectively.

Nearby yen traversed a broad daily range of more than 200 IMM ticks Friday as the contract shot up to its highest price since the March 3 high of $0.008451. Friday's peak was $0.008450, also the settlement price on February 28.
Futures have swung higher by more than 500 IMM ticks this week alone, from a low Monday at $0.007931 to Friday's high, mirroring an equally volatile cash market.

The yen's rally, predicated on ideas Japanese rates might rise and U.S. rates steady, plus jawboning by Japanese officials suggesting central banks could intervene, impressed even veteran market watchers.

"It's just a continuation of what we've had all week," said Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist, Bank of Montreal, before midday when the dollar hit its low versus the yen. "It's one of the most effective jawbonings I've seen."
He said the dollar had slumped below all his supports for the day but mentioned the 118.50 to 118.00 area as next potential dollar/yen supports.
Those cash level are roughly equivalent to $0.008482 and $0.008518, respectively, in June futures.

Comments late Thursday by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's sparked the yen rally overseas. Greenspan said he expected U.S. economic growth to slow later this year and into next but that if the economy failed to slow, "we would need to address any emerging pressures in product and credit markets."
Analysts regarded the remarks as mixed but the market viewed then as yen-syupportive.
A Japanese newspaper editorial suggesting Bank of Japan could raise rates in July fueled the steady rise in yen.

June yen surged $0.000211 to $0.008338, marks rose $0.0071 to $0.5941, Swiss francs rose $0.0114 at $0.7055, sterling was flat at $1.6212, Can dollar lost $0.0037 to $0.7204, Aus dollar lost $0.0011 to $0.7783, Mex peso fell $0.000150 to $0.124400.
